reasoning:
This issue is a follow-up decision record spun out of a Codex finding on #57 (F1-S8), not a spec'd story. It explicitly frames itself as 'Decision, not a defect' and lays out two mutually-exclusive options -- (a) add a dedicated minimal audit role holding only MANAGE GRANTS to make the PUBLIC-grant audit account-complete, or (b) accept the current DEV-visibility-scoped audit plus the pre-deploy migration scan (check_forbidden_grants.py) as sufficient best-effort coverage for a DEV environment -- without picking one. An implementing agent cannot safely choose between 'build a new privileged-ish audit role' and 'do nothing, this is already good enough' on its own; that is a real security-posture tradeoff (completeness vs. minimal-credential blast radius) squarely in the territory the operator/PM should call, exactly as the issue itself says.

Against the F1-S8 story bar: (1) Plan link -- there is none. The issue title says 'F1-S8' but the plan repo's factory.md 11 'F1 epic - stories' table only enumerates F1-S1 through F1-S6; F1-S8 does not appear there, and the issue body links to no plan.md section at all, only to other GitHub issues (#57, #11) which I cannot resolve from the ./plan-repo checkout. This isn't a self-declared dry-run/meta-issue (the F1-S6 sacrificial-dry-run exemption), so the plan-link requirement isn't waived here. (2) Acceptance criteria -- none, no checkbox list. (3) In-scope surface -- not stated; the 'options to weigh later' are alternatives, not a chosen scope. (4) Out-of-scope statement -- absent. (5) Verification notes -- absent. (6) Size declaration -- absent. None of the six readiness elements are present, and the missing plan link and undecided direction are the blocking ones -- you can't write acceptance criteria or a size declaration for a story whose two candidate outcomes are 'build a new role' vs. 'build nothing.'

Architecture-invariant note (not blocking, just flagged per the rubric): this issue is about the completeness of *detective* auditing for 'no grants to PUBLIC, anywhere,' not about weakening the invariant itself. The issue correctly notes the primary preventive control -- the pre-deploy migration scan that catches a migration-introduced GRANT ... TO PUBLIC before it's applied -- stays in place regardless of which option is chosen, and any escape is contained to the isolated DEV database. If this later becomes a real story, option (a)'s new role should be scrutinized at review time to confirm it stays read-only-for-grants and scoped only to the assert/audit connection, never merged with a broader-privilege role.

Recommend routing to a human/PM to pick a direction (or explicitly close as wontfix if best-effort is accepted) before this goes through ready-to-spec.
